1. Engagement Scope

The scope of this engagement encompasses a systematic evaluation of Arnet Pay Consulting's compensation administration practices against regulatory benchmarks established under applicable law. Field work was conducted between 2018-04-10 and 2019-06-28, with data collection spanning 308 employee records across 5 reporting units in the Character Licensing sector.

2. Methodology

Data analysis was performed using a combination of descriptive statistics, comparative analysis against Character Licensing sector benchmarks, and predictive modeling to identify outlier populations. All statistical tests were conducted at a 95% confidence level.

4. Detailed Findings
TDR-5756-001LOWOPEN
Observation

Leave administration records incomplete or contradictory for FMLA-qualifying events

Corrective Action Required

A formal USERRA compliance protocol will be integrated into the military leave of absence process, including pre-leave counseling and post-leave reemployment planning.

Management Response

While we accept the factual basis of the finding, we have performed a risk assessment and formally accepted the residual risk. This decision has been documented and approved by the Chief Risk Officer. No further corrective action is planned at this time.

Owner: Chief Strategy Officer • Due: 2018-06-28
TDR-4026-002INFORMATIONALREMEDIATED
Observation

Performance improvement plan documentation for 308 employees suggests potential disability-based bias

Corrective Action Required

Perform a root cause analysis of the EEO-1 Component 2 data errors and implement validation controls in the data preparation process to prevent recurrence in future reporting cycles.

Management Response

Management accepts the finding. The relevant system configuration has been updated, and the change will be deployed to production during the next scheduled release on 2018-04-10.

Owner: Director of Foundation Relations • Due: 2018-08-28
TDR-7920-003INFORMATIONALOPEN
Observation

Documentation gaps in personnel files for 308 employees — required for audit trail compliance

Corrective Action Required

All managers and HR personnel involved in the hiring process must complete training on compliant interviewing techniques, including prohibitions on questions related to age, disability, national origin, and other protected characteristics.

Management Response

This issue has been escalated to the executive steering committee for prioritization and resource allocation. A formal response will be provided following the committee's next scheduled meeting on 2018-04-10.

Owner: Vice President of Supply Chain • Due: 2018-07-28
TDR-9143-004LOWMONITORING
Observation

WARN Act notification timeline not met for 308 affected employees in 5 reduction-in-force

Corrective Action Required

Automate the COBRA notification process to ensure qualifying event notices are generated and mailed within 5 business days of the triggering event.

Management Response

We are awaiting final evidence of remediation from the third-party vendor responsible for this process. We have received their commitment to provide the necessary documentation by 2018-04-10 and will forward it to ACPWB upon receipt.

Owner: Vice President of Internal Audit • Due: 2018-05-28
TDR-5576-005INFORMATIONALOPEN
Observation

EU AI Act readiness assessment has not been initiated, despite the use of 308 AI-driven tools in EU hiring processes

Corrective Action Required

The company website and all subsidiary career sites will be updated to include a compliant "Your Privacy Choices" link, and a dedicated internal team will be trained to handle data subject requests.

Management Response

Management agrees with the finding. The issue has been added to the agenda for the next quarterly business review with the responsible process owners to ensure accountability.

Owner: Chief Digital Officer • Due: 2018-05-28
